keyboard.keys: Arrow Down / Arrow Up on More
keyboard.behavior: Menu opens and focuses the first/last enabled item; there is no typeahead promise.
Menu closes and returns focus to its visible toggle.
Native links and controls retain their normal activation behavior. Resize is not a focus-management policy.

guidelines: Use a sized wrapper containing a direct nav > nav-item > nav-link structure; initialize the wrapper, not the list.
Initialization runs on document ready or when loaded after parsing. Without initialization, the wrapper clips/hides the direct nav to avoid a flash. Provide your own no-script fallback when needed.
Keep items are never candidates for overflow. collapseBelow compares available wrapper width, not the viewport; named breakpoint lookup resolves once at initialization.
Overflow clones normal links and hides originals. Existing Menu nodes relocate into a submenu and are restored, preserving node identity and live input state.
A11Y-001 remaps cloned descendant IDs and local ARIA/HTML/SVG references while preserving originals; arbitrary CSS selectors and script-held references are not rewritten.
The More toggle is generated as a named native button. Custom icon input is sanitized under SEC-001; it is not arbitrary trusted HTML insertion.
update() recalculates synchronously and then dispatches update. ResizeObserver recalculates directly: it can emit overflow but does not dispatch update. resize is an internal fallback listener.
overflow is a notification with overflowCount and visibleCount, not a cancelable before gate. Restoration/recalculation can close open menus; arrange application focus deliberately.
dispose() restores original items/menus, removes the toggle item and disconnects observation. It leaves wrapper initialization classes, so do not assume it is a no-script fallback.
There is no independent overflow token map. Configure inherited Nav/Menu tokens; Toggler does not replace this component.

events.overflow.trm.navoverflow: On the wrapper after overflowing candidates; overflowCount and visibleCount describe that calculation. Notification, not a cancelable before gate.
events.resize.trm.navoverflow: Internal namespaced fallback window listener, not a dispatched component notification.
events.update.trm.navoverflow: On the wrapper after an explicit synchronous update() calculation. ResizeObserver does not dispatch update.

keyboard.behavior: Native links and controls follow document order. An open modal Drawer contains focus.
Activate the native Drawer launcher or Menu trigger.
The active Menu or Drawer handles dismissal; Navbar supplies no Escape controller.

guidelines: Use nav or a named navigation landmark and real destinations; author aria-current on the actual current link.
Include nav with navbar-nav. An always-expanded example uses navbar-expand; responsive sm:/md:/lg:navbar-expand classes use container queries.
The navbar container, not the viewport, determines expansion. Keep inner containers and test actual available width.
Responsive Drawer needs a native named dialog and Drawer JavaScript. Author initial focus and a visible close control.
Do not claim the launcher synchronizes aria-expanded: this Drawer implementation does not. aria-haspopup=dialog and aria-controls describe the relationship.
Use a separate Menu for contextual actions; Navbar has no JavaScript class or Toggler-based disclosure policy.
Close a modal Drawer before changing application layout. CSS expansion alone does not promise to release top-layer inertness or transfer focus.
Configure navbar-tokens, navbar-dark-tokens and navbar-nav-tokens. navbar-breakpoints controls generation; size lookup uses the global breakpoint helpers in this pin.
Dark navbar overrides can require explicit contrast choices in applications; the demo does not redefine core defaults.

name: toggler
title: Toggler
lead: Toggle a configured class or attribute without adding disclosure or focus policy.

variants.title: Configured class mutation
variants.description: Configuration belongs to the target. Toggle a real utility without changing visibility, ARIA or focus.
variants.markup: Always available project information.

variants.title: Remove an existing class
variants.description: The first activation removes an existing class; the next adds it. No active/pressed state is maintained on the launcher.
variants.markup: Starts highlighted.

variants.title: Self target and multiple targets
variants.description: A native button can target itself explicitly. A selector can also match multiple independent configured targets; events fire on each target.
variants.markup:
First target

Second target

variants.title: Configured attribute mutation
variants.description: Non-class attributes compare as strings: an equal value is removed, otherwise the configured value is set. This does not introduce a CSS selector or disclosure policy.
variants.markup:
Attribute target
Inspect data-count to see the numeric value set/removed.

variants.title: Native fieldset state
variants.description: A boolean disabled attribute disables native descendants. The outside launcher remains available to remove it; Toggler does not move focus or update pressed state.

variants.title: Disabled trigger
variants.description: Native disabled triggers do not activate the delegated data API.
variants.markup: Unchanged target

variants.title: Protected id and unset value
variants.description: id cannot be changed. A null or missing runtime value performs no mutation. Unless canceled, toggled still fires after these no-op paths; it is not proof of a DOM change.
variants.markup:

variants.markup: Always available project information.

keyboard.behavior: Activate an enabled native trigger. Non-native clickable elements do not gain keyboard semantics automatically.
No special behavior: targets do not hide and focus does not move.

guidelines: Configure value and optional attribute on the actual target, not only the trigger. Without a selector the trigger is its own target.
Use a single valid class token for class mutation. Multi-target selectors create/retrieve an independent instance on each matching target.
Non-class values compare as strings. Boolean HTML attributes depend on presence, so setting disabled=false still disables a native control.
The id attribute is protected; missing/null value is a no-op. A contradictory source comment does not change runtime null acceptance.
toggle.trm.toggler fires on the target before execution and is cancelable; toggled follows synchronously unless canceled, even when execution does nothing.
There is no fixed CSS class, Sass token map, className option, autoClose, dismiss, hidden, ARIA synchronization or focus policy.
Native disabled controls are ignored by the data API. Use native buttons for keyboard activation; the plugin only delegates click.
Use Collapse or native Dialog/Drawer for disclosure and modal workflows, not a Toggler compatibility shim.

example: Always available content; only its background class changes.

events.toggle.trm.toggler: Cancelable start on the configured target, before execution. Canceling prevents execution and toggled.
events.toggled.trm.toggler: Synchronous notification on the target after execution, including protected-id or null-value no-ops; not proof that an attribute changed.

sourceOptions.name: attribute
sourceOptions.description: Attribute to mutate on the target. id is protected.

sourceOptions.name: value
sourceOptions.description: One class token or the attribute value. Runtime null/missing values do nothing; the public TypeScript config excludes null.
